> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/src/security/index.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/explain-engine.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **34** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json eb4b17c346c3a82aafe09462bda3b732fa3767bf` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `65dec923a50e6edd79aafee6fbeefac00c11cf35` — the merge of head `bd7b4677773987cf5011dbde81e069167a69736e` into base `eb4b17c346c3a82aafe09462bda3b732fa3767bf`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 65dec923a50e6edd79aafee6fbeefac00c11cf35 && git checkout 65dec923a50e6edd79aafee6fbeefac00c11cf35
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin eb4b17c346c3a82aafe09462bda3b732fa3767bf bd7b4677773987cf5011dbde81e069167a69736e && git checkout -B drift-repro eb4b17c346c3a82aafe09462bda3b732fa3767bf && git merge --no-ff bd7b4677773987cf5011dbde81e069167a69736e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json eb4b17c346c3a82aafe09462bda3b732fa3767bf
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs eb4b17c346c3a82aafe09462bda3b732fa3767bf` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `bd7b4677773987cf5011dbde81e069167a69736e`
Local-runs: none

### ① Derived judgments

Inputs read: card #20580 (body and all four comments — the serial notice, the claim with its in-place Clause correction, the `os-dev-report`, the ACCEPT), PR #20614 (body, its 7-file list, the net diff against `main` at merge base `c96beb27`), and the check-runs on the head. Pre-change source was read from `origin/main` git objects only; nothing was built, run or re-run.

**Accept-set changes (runtime behaviour):**

1. `security.explain` (the service method behind the security explain route), an administrator explaining ANOTHER user, walled posture (`isolated`, `group`), the explained user holding no current membership in the caller's organization: the explained principal is now resolved with no active organization, so the caller's organization-scoped grants no longer appear in the explanation and the verdicts they decided follow enforcement's refusal. **Right.** This is enforcement's #15409 ruling-B drop applied to the explained principal — the card's direction, and no second membership rule is spelled in the explainer.
2. Same route, a CURRENT member of the caller's organization: unchanged. **Right** — the ruled KEEP pin. `vetOrganizationClaim` returns the claim when `accessible_org_ids` holds it, so `explainedTenantId === callerTenantId` and no second resolution runs.
3. `single`, or no posture supplied: unchanged on both faces. **Right** — the function returns the claim before consulting memberships.
4. A caller with no active organization (`callerTenantId` undefined): unchanged. **Right** — the vet returns `undefined`, equal to its input, so no rebuild; the explained user is still resolved with no organization, as on `main`.
5. Explaining oneself, or a request with no `userId`: unchanged. **Right** — the whole edit sits inside the `request.userId !== callerContext.userId` arm (read at `security-plugin.ts` about L4690–4735 on `main`); the `manage_users` / delegated-scope gate ahead of it is untouched.
6. `resolveAuthzContext` session arm: no behaviour change. **Right, verified at source.** Old predicate: `!keyPrincipal && tenantId && input.tenancyPosture && postureEnforcesWall(input.tenancyPosture) && !grants.accessible_org_ids.includes(tenantId)`. New: `!keyPrincipal && tenantId && vetOrganizationClaim(tenantId, grants.accessible_org_ids, input.tenancyPosture) === undefined`. With `tenantId` truthy under the guard, `vetOrganizationClaim` returns the claim (truthy, so not `undefined`) when the posture is absent or walls nothing, and returns `undefined` exactly when the posture walls and the claim is absent from the set — the same truth table on every input. The existing test file gains one import and one new describe block; no existing case is edited.
7. The vet's input is the right set. `accessible_org_ids` is built in `resolveUserAuthzGrants` from `sys_member` rows filtered by `user_id` alone (Leg 1, `main` about L757–802), never by the `tenantId` the grants were resolved in — so vetting against the context built in the caller's organization asks exactly the membership set enforcement asks. The new TSDoc's statement to that effect is accurate.
8. Posture input: the explainer passes `this.tenancyPosture` (the plugin's read of the `tenancy` service); enforcement passes the admission seam's read of the same service. Equal whenever a `tenancy` service is registered; the no-service composition is the dev's finding 2, escalated in ③.
9. The API-key arm (`main` about L454–470) is untouched, and rightly so — its consequence is a refusal to NO PRINCIPAL (#15256 2A), not a drop; a separately ruled decision outside this card.

**Public-surface changes:**

10. `@objectstack/core` gains `vetOrganizationClaim(claimedOrganizationId, accessibleOrgIds, tenancyPosture)` on `security/index.ts`, reaching the root barrel through its `export * from './security/index.js'`, and from there `@objectstack/runtime` and `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server` through their `export * from '@objectstack/core'`. Additive; zero prior occurrences of the name anywhere on `main`, so no `export *` ambiguity. **Right.** Core has no exported-surface snapshot gate (its `check:` scripts are `check:test-typecheck` only), so no generated artifact is owed.
11. `buildContextForUser` and `explainAccessForCaller` signatures unchanged; `explain-engine.ts` is a four-line doc edit. **Right** — the A4 reading holds.
12. No `packages/spec` path, no REST route, no governed path, no env var: no artifact regeneration, no closed query-parameter set, and no tier record beyond this one is owed. Governed Surface Queue Guard: success. Head repo is the base repo; 438 changed lines, under the human-merge threshold.

**Scope against the claim `5885265359`:** all seven paths are inside the named file surface. The `packages/core/src/security/**` exception was correctly triggered — the session arm's predicate was inline and reachable only through `resolveAuthzContext` itself, which would skip the explainer's ruled grants-cache bypass and write a false dropped-claim log line. `postureEnforcesWall` was already imported by the plugin, so an inline spelling was possible, but it is exactly the "second membership rule" the card forbids. The exception's three conditions hold: no behaviour change (item 6), a cross-lane notice (`5886089080`, per the ACCEPT), and Clause-② re-judged (②).

**Pin quality:** `explain-removed-member-principal.test.ts` is a parity pin, not a fixed-value pin — every case compares the explanation with enforcement's own resolution and read over the same rows (a real ObjectQL on two drivers, the real `SecurityPlugin`, `resolveAuthzContext` then `assembleExecutionContext` then a middleware `find`). Negative pins (removed member: set absent, `object_crud` denies, own read 403 `PERMISSION_DENIED`), KEEP pins (current member unchanged, granted on both faces), a `single` control, and a precondition that the set is resolvable at all, so a negative pin cannot pass for want of a grant. 22 cases = 2 drivers × (2 postures × 5 + 1 control), matching the report; the ablation's 8 red = 2 drivers × 2 postures × 2 removed-member pins, matching. Imports are package imports with no filesystem escape, so `check:cross-package-test-inputs` has nothing to see. The report's core measurements were taken at `cf18f3e99`; the delta from there to the head is 11 lines in the pin file alone, as stated.

**Check-runs on the head, as read:** success — Build Core, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Check Changeset, Type Check · debt ledger, Type Check · source gates, Dogfood Regression Gate (3/3), Dogfood Verify CLI, Check PR Size, Check Documentation Links, Flag docs affected by code changes, the five PR-shape guards (branch claim, single-writer path, same issue, part-of), filter, Auto Label. in_progress — Test Core (1/6 through 6/6), Dogfood Regression Gate (1/3, 2/3), Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL), Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · workspace, Lint & Repo Gates. skipped — Console Pin Gate (an additive change, nothing for the pinned sibling to lose), Build Docs, Packed-tarball smoke. No failure at the time of reading. The seat checks convergence before landing; this verdict judges ①②③.

### ② Semver level

Changeset `.changeset/20580-explain-removed-member.md`: `@objectstack/core: minor`, `@objectstack/plugin-security: patch`. This matches what the diff publishes — one new export on core (a widening, so at least `minor`), and a behaviour fix with no signature change on plugin-security (`patch`). Not breaking: nothing is removed or renamed, so no ADR-0087 marker and no FROM → TO migration is owed, and the changeset correctly carries no Clause line (that line rides in a changeset only beside a breaking marker). Not naming `runtime` / `plugin-hono-server` for the reached additive name is within precedent (mixed; the fixed group moves them together anyway). The body describes the fix, the export with its signature and return contract, and the unchanged set. Check Changeset: success.

Clause-②: yes (widening)

That is the PR body's line as corrected by the seat from `no`, and this record agrees with the correction: the dev's original `no` was wrong once the core export existed, the seat's in-place correction of claim and body is the right act, and `yes` is consistent with the `minor` grade.

### ③ Boundary flags

**Dev deviations (`os-dev-report` `5886046353`):**

1. A2 — a core export instead of a plugin-local rule. **Accepted.** Within the claim's exception; equivalence verified (① item 6); the alternative callers were rightly rejected. Cross-lane notice recorded by the ACCEPT.
2. Widening / Clause-② — **Accepted and closed** by the seat's correction (②). The changeset carrying no Clause line is correct for a non-breaking changeset.
3. A4 not triggered — **Confirmed** by the diff: `buildContextForUser` is doc-only.
4. A1 / A3 confirmed — **Confirmed** by the pin's precondition (enforcement drops the removed member's claim and keeps the current member's) and by the `single` control.
5. sqlite-only drivers, no PG leg — **Accepted.** The compared question (membership-set membership under a posture) is above the dialect; the rig's fixed platform-table ids justify avoiding a shared server. Enforcement's own PG coverage lives in its own suites.
6. Probe object platform-global so Layer 0 stays out — **Accepted**; it isolates the grant-driven verdict this card rules on. The tenant-object position is finding 1.
7. `main` not merged before opening — **Accepted, no action**: the three intervening commits touch `rest`, spec comments and `plugin-audit`, disjoint from every path and package here; CI on the head and the queue's rebuilt generation validate the merge (Multi-agent discipline §10).

**Open question (finding 1 — the explained context carries no organization of its own):** **A, as the seat answered** (`5886097649`). Fixing it here would change a current member's explanation, which this card's ruled KEEP pin holds unchanged; #20604 owns every explain-versus-enforce position with an enumeration pin. Not re-ruled here.

**Out-of-scope findings:**

- Entry 1 (class a, same reach, measured on two positions) — **Carried by #20604** per the ACCEPT. A real defect with a named landing site, so Prime Directive #10 is satisfied by the carrier rather than a single-point card.
- Entry 2 (posture-source asymmetry with no `tenancy` service; a read-only inference) — **Noted on #20604, correctly not filed**: a card names measured evidence, and this has none yet. From this review's reading: the explainer reads `this.tenancyPosture`, which the plugin can resolve to `isolated` from an `org-scoping` probe when no `tenancy` service exists, while admission hands the resolver no posture in that composition — so the two faces could disagree there. Same carrier.

**Reviewer findings (this record's own, none verdict-bearing):**

- R1, doc accuracy: the new export's TSDoc says nothing else spells this rule and a caller that needs it calls this. The API-key arm of the same file (`main` about L456) still spells `postureEnforcesWall(posture) && !grants.accessible_org_ids.includes(keyPrincipal.tenantId)` inline, with a different consequence (refusal, #15256 2A). Leaving that arm alone was right for this card; the sentence is overstated. Follow-up for the #20604 family: either route the key arm's predicate through `vetOrganizationClaim` as a no-behaviour-change refactor, or narrow the sentence to the session arm. No runtime string, no gate and no behaviour turns on it.
- R2: `explained.accessible_org_ids ?? []` guards a field `buildContextForUser` always sets to an array (its return is untyped, so the guard is not forced by a type). Dead in practice; if it ever fired it would fail closed (the claim dropped under a wall). Not a Prime Directive #12 alias — no metadata dialect is tolerated — so accepted as written.
- R3: the dropped-claim case pays a second `resolveUserAuthzGrants` with the ruled cache bypass. Only a stale claim reaches it; acceptable.
